prompt.adult: Psalm 1 contrasts the blessed man with others. In 1:4, what are they like?
prompt.child: Psalm 1 says people who do not follow God are like something the wind blows away. What?
prompt.teen: Psalm 1:4: “But are like ___ which the wind drives away.” What fills the blank?
prompt.older: According to Psalm 1:4, what are those who do not walk with God like?

verses.text: The ungodly are not so, But are like the chaff which the wind drives away.

explanation.child: Look at the end of verse 4.
explanation.teen: 1:4 opens with a contrast and then gives a picture. Read it.
explanation.older: It is near the end of 1:4, before “which the wind.”

teaching.extended_explanation: 1:4 opens with a contrast with the blessed man of 1:1-3. 1:5 adds that they shall not stand in the judgment.
teaching.takeaway: They are like the chaff which the wind drives away.

prompt.adult: “Do not fret because of evildoers.” In 37:11, who shall inherit the earth and delight in the abundance of peace?
prompt.child: Psalm 37 says some people will inherit the earth. Who are they?
prompt.teen: Psalm 37:11: “But ___ shall inherit the earth.” Who fills the blank?
prompt.older: According to Psalm 37:11, who shall inherit the earth?

verses.text: But the meek shall inherit the earth, And shall delight themselves in the abundance of peace.

explanation.child: Look at the start of verse 11.
explanation.teen: 37:11 names a group and then says what they will enjoy. Read the group.

teaching.extended_explanation: 37:10 says that in a little while the wicked shall be no more. 37:11 adds that this group shall delight themselves in the abundance of peace.

review.notes: Fruitful stage. NKJV excerpt copied from _fruitful_nkjv.json (BibleGateway NKJV). Answer is in the cited verse.

prompt.adult: In 37:23, what does the psalmist say about the steps of a good man?
prompt.child: Psalm 37 talks about the steps a good person takes. What does it say about them?
prompt.teen: Psalm 37:23: “The steps of a good man are ___.” What fills the blank?
prompt.older: According to Psalm 37:23, what is true of a good man’s steps?

verses.text: The steps of a good man are ordered by the LORD, And He delights in his way.
Though he fall, he shall not be utterly cast down; For the LORD upholds him with His hand.

explanation.child: Look at the start of verse 23.
explanation.teen: 37:23 has two lines. Read the end of the first.
explanation.older: It closes the first line of 37:23.

teaching.extended_explanation: 37:23 adds that the LORD delights in his way. 37:24 says that though he fall, he shall not be utterly cast down, for the LORD upholds him with His hand.
teaching.takeaway: His steps are “ordered by the LORD.”

prompt.adult: “Do not be afraid when one becomes rich.” In 49:17, what shall he carry when he dies?
prompt.child: Psalm 49 says not to worry when someone gets rich. What can a rich man take with him when he dies?
prompt.teen: Psalm 49:17: “For when he dies he shall carry ___.” What fills the blank?
prompt.older: According to Psalm 49:17, what does the rich man carry with him at death?

verses.text: Do not be afraid when one becomes rich, When the glory of his house is increased;
For when he dies he shall carry nothing away; His glory shall not descend after him.

explanation.child: Look at the start of verse 17.
explanation.teen: 49:16 gives the command; 49:17 gives the reason. Read its first line.
explanation.older: It ends the first line of 49:17.

teaching.extended_explanation: 49:16 tells of the glory of his house increased. 49:18-19 add that men praise him while he lives, yet he shall go to the generation of his fathers.
teaching.takeaway: When he dies he shall carry nothing away.

prompt.adult: The prosperity of the wicked was too painful for the psalmist to understand. In 73:17, where did he go before he understood their end?
prompt.child: The writer of Psalm 73 was upset that bad people seemed to do well. Where did he go that helped him understand?
prompt.teen: Psalm 73:17: “Until I went” where? “Then I understood their end.”
prompt.older: According to Psalm 73:17, where was the psalmist when he understood the end of the wicked?

choices.text: into the courts of the king

verses.text: When I thought how to understand this, It was too painful for me—
Until I went into the sanctuary of God; Then I understood their end.

explanation.child: Look at the start of verse 17.
explanation.teen: 73:16 tells of the struggle; 73:17 says where it changed. Read the first line.

teaching.extended_explanation: 73:16 says that thinking about it was too painful. 73:18 goes on: “Surely You set them in slippery places.”
teaching.takeaway: He went “into the sanctuary of God.”

review.notes: Fruitful stage. NKJV excerpt copied from _fruitful_nkjv.json (BibleGateway NKJV). Answer is in the cited verse.

prompt.adult: In 73:2 the psalmist’s feet had almost stumbled. In 112:7, of what will the righteous man not be afraid?
prompt.child: Psalm 112 says a person who trusts God has a steady heart. What does he not fear?
prompt.teen: Psalm 112:7: “He will not be afraid of ___.” What fills the blank?
prompt.older: According to Psalm 112:7, what will the righteous man not fear?

verses.text: But as for me, my feet had almost stumbled; My steps had nearly slipped.
He will not be afraid of evil tidings; His heart is steadfast, trusting in the LORD.

explanation.child: Look at the start of verse 7.
explanation.teen: 73:2 is the setting; 112:7 has two lines. Read the end of the first.
explanation.older: It closes the first line of 112:7.

teaching.extended_explanation: 73:2 says his steps had nearly slipped. 112:7 gives the reason the righteous man stands firm: “His heart is steadfast, trusting in the LORD.”
teaching.takeaway: He will not be afraid of evil tidings.

prompt.adult: Psalm 1:2 tells when the blessed man meditates. According to 37:30, what does the mouth of the righteous do?
prompt.child: Psalm 37 describes what a good person’s mouth does. What does it do?
prompt.teen: Psalm 37:30: “The mouth of the righteous” does what?
prompt.older: Alongside the blessed man of Psalm 1:2, what does Psalm 37:30 say the mouth of the righteous does?

verses.text: But his delight is in the law of the LORD, And in His law he meditates day and night.
The mouth of the righteous speaks wisdom, And his tongue talks of justice.

explanation.child: Look at the start of Psalm 37:30.
explanation.teen: 1:2 is the setting; 37:30 has two lines, one for the mouth and one for the tongue. Read the first.
explanation.older: It closes the first line of 37:30.

teaching.extended_explanation: 1:2 says when the blessed man meditates. 37:30 sets the mouth beside the tongue in two matching lines.
teaching.takeaway: The mouth of the righteous speaks wisdom.

prompt.adult: Psalm 49:20 describes a man in honor who does not understand. In 73:22, how does the psalmist describe himself when he was foolish and ignorant?
prompt.child: In Psalm 73 the writer admits he was foolish. What did he say he was like before God?
prompt.teen: Psalm 73:22: “I was so foolish and ignorant; I was like” what?
prompt.older: Psalm 49:20 describes a man who does not understand. According to 73:22, what was the psalmist like before God?

verses.text: A man who is in honor, yet does not understand, Is like the beasts that perish.
I was so foolish and ignorant; I was like a beast before You.

explanation.child: Look at the last words of Psalm 73:22.
explanation.teen: 49:20 is the setting; 73:22 is the confession. Read the end of it.

teaching.extended_explanation: 49:20 ends Psalm 49 with a comparison for the one who is in honor yet does not understand. 73:23 follows the confession at once: “Nevertheless I am continually with You.”
teaching.takeaway: He was “like a beast before You.”
